correctness.rationale: For every m,r>=2, f_a^m is the internal r-rotation by one, implying a single mr-cycle and shift-independent all-time signs. Conversely, an arbitrary matching cycle f has g=f^m with m length-r cycles and exactly the m block endpoints as descent points. Every cycle maximum descends; equality of number of descents and cycles forces each consecutive block as one g-cycle. Increasing displacement outside the block maximum forces its unique rotation. Commutation forces f to send whole blocks to blocks; time-one inequalities force consecutive block order. Intertwining of rotations makes each interblock map a cyclic translation, and f^m=g imposes sum of shifts one. Thus exactly r^(m-1) cycles, including m=r=2 boundaries. Complete exhaustion of all n-cycles for n=4,6,8,9,10 confirms eight instances but does not replace this proof.

value.rationale: The motivating work identifies prime-cycle uniqueness versus composite ambiguity without quantifying it. The theorem supplies an exact, structurally classified ambiguity fiber for every composite factorization, including exponentially many indistinguishable cycles at even periods despite all time/point observations. It is a nontrivial converse inverse-identifiability result, not a mere special numerical substitution or an arbitrary census.
